ADR-0136-amendment.title: Foundry scope clarification — INTERNAL only
ADR-0136-amendment.decision: Foundry µservice (microservices/foundry/) is INTERNAL ONLY — Hermes agentic dev toolchain, CI/CD orchestration, internal eval, internal evidence collection. NOT consumer-facing. Consumer AI = separate µservice microservices/intelligence/ per ADR-0220.
ADR-0136-amendment.rationale: User directive 2026-05-18: 'Foundry is internal tool. oyatie intelligence + ontology + workflow is consumer facing.' Past session work incorrectly framed Foundry agents as consumer-facing (e.g., 'Foundry-powered 1:1 prep AI'). Those references corrected to 'oyatie intelligence' in this amendment.
impacts: Past references to 'Foundry agents for HR Q&A / 1:1 prep / management-cockpit insights' → corrected to 'oyatie intelligence'
Milvus (ADR-0192) serves BOTH Foundry (internal eval corpora) AND oyatie intelligence (per-tenant RAG); per-cell logical isolation
Wasmtime (ADR-0200) serves BOTH (internal tool sandboxing in Foundry; tenant context sandboxing in intelligence)

ADR-0211.title: In-house tech stack policy
ADR-0211.status: ACCEPTED — already cited as accepted in v3 audit; orphan citation that must be resolved
ADR-0211.decision_summary: Wherever possible, oyatie supports an in-house tech stack — like AWS, Google, Microsoft, Oracle. Component classification rubric: (a) Community-standard / CNCF-graduated → KEEP, adapter for swap, no Phase-2 in-house replacement (these ARE the standards). (b) Vendor-replaceable → Phase-0 adapter wrapper + Phase-2 in-house native build with value-anchored trigger (NOT date-anchored). (c) In-house mandatory (our differentiation) → 100% in-house from day 1.

community_standard_KEEP: Prometheus / Mimir / Loki / Tempo / Grafana / OTel / AlertManager — all CNCF
OIDC / WebAuthn L3 / SCIM 2.0 — IETF/W3C standards

vendor_replaceable_with_phase_2_native.trigger: ≥50K tenants per pack OR multi-region active-active RTO ≤30s requirement Zitadel can't natively support
≥1B vectors per cluster OR Foundry/intelligence RAG latency budget breached
≥100TB per tenant OR cross-tenant isolation breach
≥1PB cluster OR multi-region active-active write coordination need
≥1M sends/day/tenant × 7d sustained OR sovereign air-gap deploy
Backstage scope exceeded for service catalog + TechDocs
≥10K nodes per workflow OR svelte-flow performance ceiling
BUSL enterprise tier requirement OR Meilisearch licensing concern escalation

in_house_mandatory_differentiation: Foundry (internal Hermes agentic substrate per ADR-0136 amendment)
Audit Chain (Ed25519 + Merkle per Bominal ADR-0028)
Consent Graph (per ADR-0214 — cross-tenant visibility moat)
Plugin App Store + Developer SDK (per ADR-0213 — ecosystem moat)
Compliance evidence pipeline (Drata/Vanta-replacement; built in-house from day 1)

ADR-0212.title: Buildability Doctrine
ADR-0212.decision_summary: Every artifact (PRDs, ADRs, IPs, runbooks, contracts, Helm charts, SLOs, standards docs) must be self-sufficient enough that a stranger (new engineer or AI agent) walks up cold and produces production-ready hyperscaler-grade output WITHOUT tribal knowledge. No false signals. No padding.

per_artifact_bar.PRD: 5+ user stories with measurable acceptance criteria; explicit scope-in/scope-out; success metrics with numbers; trace to phases
per_artifact_bar.PHASE-SPEC: Phases list IPs; each IP has owner, blocking deps, exit criteria
per_artifact_bar.IP: ≥150 SUBSTANTIVE lines; file-level paths; line ranges; test count + names; evidence to emit; idempotency; rollback steps; NOT padded filler
per_artifact_bar.ADR: Context + Decision + ≥3 alternatives with rejected-because + ≥3 consequences (positive + negative + operational) + named industry sources + §'In-house roadmap'
per_artifact_bar.Contract: Sufficient to generate working clients in TS/Rust/Swift/Kotlin/C#/Python; ≥3 worked examples per endpoint; idempotency-key + cursor pagination + X-Request-Id + ULID baked in
per_artifact_bar.Helm_chart: Deploys working substrate; per-pack overlays; OpenBao SecretReference for secrets; values fully documented
per_artifact_bar.Runbook: Step-by-step executable as-is; no 'ask SME' steps; named commands; expected outputs; rollback at every step
per_artifact_bar.SLO: Concrete numerical targets; burn-rate alerts wired (4-window per ADR-0139); dashboards linked
per_artifact_bar.Threat_model: STRIDE per surface; named specific attack vectors (not abstract)
per_artifact_bar.Standards_doc: Implementable from doc alone; no 'see X for details' hand-waves

ADR-0212.ci_enforcement_gate: oya-check-buildability-discipline (advisory mode initially → BLOCKER once 33+ µservices pass)

ADR-0215.title: Multi-Context Platform Architecture
ADR-0215.decision_summary: One human principal can carry multiple data contexts simultaneously: work-context-{employer-X, employer-Y…} + personal-context + healthcare-patient-context + healthcare-provider-context + education-student-context + government-citizen-context. Each context has independent data scope, governance, audit chain, sovereignty. Cross-context bridges only via consent-graph (ADR-0214) — explicit user grants. Same Connect family µservice (mail, messenger, calendar, social, docs, sheets, etc.) handles ALL contexts with strict data partitioning.
implementations: identity µservice extension: multi-context principal resolver (Fix-Q's existing identity µservice extended)
Connect family µservices: data partitioning per context with shared UI
Cedar policy: context-aware authorization (work-context Cedar fragments differ from personal-context)
Audit chain: per-context sealed audit trail
comparable_implementations: Apple Managed Apple ID vs personal Apple ID
Google Workspace vs personal Google account
Microsoft M365 work account vs personal Outlook.com

ADR-0216.title: Open Integration & Migration-Out Policy
ADR-0216.decision_summary: Lock-in is FORBIDDEN. Trust via openness is the moat. Every µservice ships: (1) first-party importer FROM top-3 competitors; (2) first-party exporter TO top-3 competitors; (3) OpenAPI 3.2.0 + AsyncAPI 3.1.0 + proto3 contracts as canonical surface; (4) plugin extension points via Wasmtime sandbox + plugin-app-store; (5) open-standards (OIDC/SCIM/SAML/FHIR/ISO 20022/xBRL/OpenAPI/OpenSLO/OpenTofu/FOCUS) compliance. Customers know they CAN leave → they aren't afraid to start → they start → they adopt more → they don't leave. Paradoxical lock-in via trust.
comparable_implementations: Apple ecosystem (open enough — third-party apps + iCloud + Apple Pay)
Google Workspace (one account, but open APIs)

ADR-0217.title: Vertical Slice Rollout Order
ADR-0217.decision_summary: Plan all µservices in PR-143; ROLLOUT to production-GA one vertical at a time. Each vertical must reach hyperscaler-grade depth before next vertical starts. Vertical depth + completeness > horizontal breadth.

vertical_order.why: Largest revenue surface; best cross-product integration test; medium compliance bar
Highest compliance bar (HIPAA + Joint Commission + state DPH); regulatory-pack stress test; Epic/Cerner FHIR connector validation; multi-context platform stress test
B2C marketplace + commerce stack validation; payments at scale; consumer surfaces stress test
Mass-market; simpler onboarding; ease-of-adoption claim test
ERP integration + IoT; sector data model density
Route optimization + fleet + consent-graph real-time visibility stress test
Highest combined regulatory bar (KYC/AML/SOC2/PCI-DSS); fintech market
FedRAMP High + state procurement; longest sales cycle; highest trust bar

ADR-0218.title: Tenant Granular Control Surface
ADR-0218.decision_summary: Tenants (organizations) get granular control over: (a) tenant-authored Cedar policy fragments (own scope; composes with platform-base-deny); (b) tenant-defined custom roles (beyond platform default enum); (c) tenant-scoped data_class extensions; (d) tenant-admin access management UI in Application B2B shell; (e) tenant-self-serve JIT access grants for contractors; (f) tenant-authored approval workflows via Workflow Studio templates; (g) per-product, per-role, per-data-class permission matrix.
tenant_admin_console_capabilities: Access policies (Cedar fragments authored in visual builder)
Audit visibility (per-tenant audit-log slicing per ADR-0162)
API keys per tier + per-purpose (Stripe pattern)
ADR-0218.substrate_existing: Cedar policy engine (ADR-0150/0183), SCIM 2.0 inbound (ADR-0190), identity OIDC + WebAuthn (ADR-0187/0188), per-tenant audit-log slicing (ADR-0162), per-tenant env tiers (ADR-0163), Application B2B shell (ADR-0061), tenancy RLS + JWT + cells
ADR-0218.ux_layer_needed: Visual builders in Application B2B shell (Tenant Admin Console) — extends Application µservice with no-code-first surfaces per ADR-0219

ADR-0219.title: No-Code-First UX with Optional AI-Assist
ADR-0219.decision_summary: Most professional tasks must be possible WITHOUT technical knowledge. Visual deterministic builders are PRIMARY UX (no code, no SQL, no JSON, no CLI). AI-assist via Foundry+intelligence is OPT-IN accelerator for genuinely fuzzy/semantic tasks. Programmatic Workflow + Ontology + Cedar paths handle deterministic flows without AI in the loop. Don't waste AI on deterministic tasks (cost + latency + fallibility). Don't weaken UX in either direction — both paths coexist.
deterministic_patterns_no_ai: Build a workflow (drag-and-drop canvas — svelte-flow per ADR-0204)
Build a report (drag-and-drop dimensions/measures — Looker pattern)
Define a role (visual selection of products × scopes × actions)
Issue API key per environment tier (form-based UI — Stripe pattern)
Audit query (faceted filter UI — Splunk pattern)
Edit a Cedar policy for simple cases (visual matrix builder)
Enable a product à-la-carte (one click — ADR-0061)
doctrine_rules: Visual builder is primary; AI button is opt-in
AI drafts render INTO the visual builder so user reviews + edits in same UI
AI output is always a DRAFT for human review, never auto-applied
Cost discipline: AI tokens spent only on user invocation; no shadow agent loops
Developer API/SDK/CLI access exists for those who choose it

ADR-0220.title: Consumer Intelligence Substrate (microservices/intelligence/)
ADR-0220.decision_summary: microservices/intelligence/ is the CONSUMER-FACING AI substrate (B2B tenants + B2C personal users), distinct from microservices/foundry/ which is INTERNAL ONLY (Hermes agentic dev pipeline). Brand label shown to users: 'oyatie intelligence' — similar to Apple Intelligence / Microsoft Copilot / Google AI / WeChat super-app AI. Lives WITHIN every consumer product (Workflow Studio, HR, Payroll, Connect family, marketplace, etc.) as the AI surface backed by this µservice.
ownership: Cross-product AI orchestration (an HR question that traverses payroll + comp data)
Model routing (which model, which provider, which tier)
Cost attribution per-tenant for AI tokens
Consent management for AI usage (opt-out support)
EU AI Act Annex III high-risk classification tracking per capability tier
DSAR compliance (AI memory deletion on user request)
Audit chain for AI decisions (GDPR Art. 22 automated decision-making transparency)
substrate_shared_with_foundry: Milvus vector DB (per-cell logical isolation; intelligence = per-tenant RAG; Foundry = internal eval corpora)
Wasmtime sandbox (per ADR-0200; intelligence = tenant context sandboxing; Foundry = internal tool sandboxing)
Same underlying runtime; separated by µservice + cell + tenant boundaries
ADR-0220.naming: µservice path microservices/intelligence/ (no 'oyatie-' prefix per convention); crate prefix oya-intelligence-*-{kernel,domain,usecase,api,adapter,rest,worker,sdk,app}; brand label 'oyatie intelligence' shown to users
